What makes London residential refurbishment different

Almost every London residential refurbishment happens in an occupied or shared building. Mansion blocks in Kensington, Chelsea, Mayfair, St John's Wood and Belgravia have their own alterations rules, hours-of-work windows, goods-lift booking systems, protection requirements for marble common parts, and named acoustic performance targets in the lease. A refurbishment programme that ignores those is a fight with the managing agent that eats weeks and eats the client's goodwill.

The licence-to-alter process with the freeholder is a parallel programme. Full licence-to-alter with structural works can take 8 to 16 weeks to obtain, involves the freeholder's surveyor, and typically requires a set of contract drawings, a method statement, insurance evidence and a fee. We include the licence-to-alter process in the pre-construction programme so it does not blindside the works.

Frequently asked questions

What is a licence to alter?

A written consent from the freeholder (usually via their surveyor) allowing a leaseholder to carry out alterations to the demised premises. Typically required for any structural works, MEP alterations that penetrate the demise, and often even for internal replanning. The licence sets out approved drawings, insurance, hours of work, method statement and a fee. Works started before licence is granted are a lease breach and expose the leaseholder to enforcement.

Do you deal with the freeholder and managing agent?

Yes. We deal directly with the freeholder's surveyor, the managing agent and the block's concierge or porters. Every arrival, delivery, hoisting slot and out-of-hours works permission is agreed in writing and logged, so the client is not the one having the daily conversation with the porters.

How long does a whole-house refurbishment take?

A three-bedroom flat in a mansion block: typically 16 to 26 weeks on site, plus 8 to 16 weeks for licence-to-alter. A four-to-six-bedroom townhouse: 30 to 52 weeks on site depending on the extent of restructure. Programmes include contingency for licence-to-alter, party wall and building control inspection windows.

What VAT rate applies?

The standard 20% VAT rate applies to most residential refurbishment. A reduced 5% rate applies to qualifying works on a dwelling that has been empty for at least two years, and to certain qualifying energy-saving measures. Zero rating applies to certain works on newly constructed dwellings and to certain approved alterations for disabled use. We flag the applicable rate at tender.

What warranties are provided?

Manufacturer warranties on kitchen, bathroom, appliance and MEP products; installer warranties on plumbing, electrical, heating and cooling installations; and a 12-month defects rectification period under the contract. Extended warranties on structural elements are provided on request via IWA, ICW or an insurance-backed guarantee.

How is snagging handled?

A snagging walk is done with the client and the design team, and a snag list is issued. Snags are cleared before or shortly after handover. A second snag walk is offered around six months into the rectification period. Defects arising after handover are handled through a single point of contact for the 12-month rectification period.
